title: Defensive Design, Validation and Testing
intro: A short, independent catch-up: learn the essential knowledge, practise and review answers.

questions.prompt: What is the first valid index of an array in these OCR ERL examples?
questions.feedback: Arrays in these lessons use zero-based indexes.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the explanations, visual and model before answering.

blocks.title: Robust programs
blocks.text: Defensive design anticipates invalid or malicious input and uses readable, maintainable code.

blocks.title: Validation
blocks.text: Validation checks input against rules such as type, length or range. It does not verify a person's identity.

blocks.title: Authentication
blocks.text: Authentication establishes identity, for example using credentials or another factor.

blocks.title: Testing
blocks.text: Use normal, boundary, invalid and erroneous values; compare expected and actual results. Test during development and again at the end.

blocks.title: Visual model
blocks.caption: Use these linked concepts to explain your answer.

blocks.title: Worked example · A program accepts a mark from 0 to 100 inclusive. Choose test data and explain the expected results.
blocks.text: Write the validation rule: 0 <= mark <= 100. Choose normal data: 56 → accepted. Choose boundary data: 0 and 100 → accepted. Choose invalid data of the correct type: -1 or 101 → rejected. Choose erroneous data of the wrong type, e.g. 'hello' → rejected or handled safely.

items: defensive design — Designing programs to handle invalid input and misuse.
validation — Checking entered data against defined rules.
boundary data — Valid data at the extreme limits of an allowed range.

questions.prompt: For an inclusive mark range 0–100, which input is invalid?
questions.feedback: 101 is just above the valid upper boundary.
